section.title: Writing an Equation to Represent a Real-World Problems
section.para: Here are the steps to writing an equation to represent a real-world scenario:

div.para:
Step 1 - Read the problem.
Step 2 - Identify the variables and known values. If needed, sketch a picture of the scenario.
Step 3 - Write a sentence using the relationship among the values.
Step 4 - Translate the sentence into an equation.

section.title: Example
section.para: Write the following statement algebraically using symbols: Peanuts cost $3.59 per pound. Max buys \(p\) pounds of peanuts and pays $10.77.
Peanuts cost $3.59 per pound. Max buys \(p\) pounds of peanuts and pays $10.77.
Step 2 - Identify the variables and known values. If needed, sketch a picture of the scenario.
\(p\) = number of pounds of peanuts bought
Step 3 - Write a sentence using the relationship among the values.
The cost per pound times the number of pounds bought equals the total cost of peanuts
Step 4 - Translate the sentence into an equation.
section.title: Try It: Writing an Equation to Represent a Real-World Problem

div.para: Translate the following scenario into an equation:
A married couple together earns $110,000 a year. The wife earns $16,000 less than twice what her husband earns. What does the husband earn?
Together the husband and wife earn $110,000 a year.
The wife earns $16,000 less than twice what her husband earns.

list.item: After reading the problem, what are some of the known variables identified in the description?

div.para: \( h \) = the amount the husband earns.

list.item: Identify a variable and describe what it represents for this scenario.

div.para: Together the husband and wife earn $110,000.

list.item: What sentence can be used to describe the relationship among the values?
What equation can be used to represent the scenario?
